pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: mm: split page_type out from _mapcount We're already using a union of many fields here, so stop abusing the _mapcount and make page_type its own field. That implies renaming some of the machinery that creates PageBuddy, PageBalloon and PageKmemcg; bring back the PG_buddy, PG_balloon and PG_kmemcg names. As suggested by Kirill, make page_type a bitmask. Because it starts out life as -1 (thanks to sharing the storage with _mapcount), setting a page flag means clearing the appropriate bit. This gives us space for probably twenty or so extra bits (depending how paranoid we want to be about _mapcount underflow). UPSTREAM: mm: mark pages in use for page tables Define a new PageTable bit in the page_type and use it to mark pages in use as page tables. This can be helpful when debugging crashdumps or analysing memory fragmentation. Add a KPF flag to report these pages to userspace and update page-types.c to interpret that flag. Note that only pages currently accounted as NR_PAGETABLES are tracked as PageTable; this does not include pgd/p4d/pud/pmd pages. Those will be the subject of a later patch. UPSTREAM: mm: mmu_notifier fix for tlb_end_vma The generic tlb_end_vma does not call invalidate_range mmu notifier, and it resets resets the mmu_gather range, which means the notifier won't be called on part of the range in case of an unmap that spans multiple vmas. ARM64 seems to be the only arch I could see that has notifiers and uses the generic tlb_end_vma. I have not actually tested it. [ Catalin and Will point out that ARM64 currently only uses the notifiers for KVM, which doesn't use the ->invalidate_range() callback right now, so it's a bug, but one that happens to not affect them. So not necessary for stable. - Linus ] Signed-off-by: Nicholas Piggin <npiggin@gmail.com> Acked-by: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com> Acked-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com> Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> (cherry picked from commit fd1102f0aadec7d18792b132e1d224290b2aecca) BUG=b:123039911 TEST=Built Change-Id: I6198d5887cbf6b8ef663aca5ff4b0915fe03bd79 Signed-off-by: Yu Zhao <yuzhao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1464388 Tested-by: Yu Zhao <yuzhao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Yu Zhao <yuzhao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yu Zhao <yuzhao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: mm: kstaled: a kswapd alternative kstaled differs from kswapd in the following respects: 1) kstaled walks page tables directly to clear the accessed bit on PTE. This allows kstaled to track the accesses of all mapped pages with even less CPU overhead comparing with the rmap. 2) kstaled stores a N-bit age, i.e., timestamp of the last access, for each page and sorts pages based on the age. This is a closer approximation to the LRU, which reduces swap refaults. 3) kstaled scans at a fixed interval to prevent thrashing. If it can't produce enough cold pages for reclaim to consume, allocation will be throttled to allow the tab discarder to take action. BUG=b:123039911 TEST=Ran platform.MemoryPressure and platform.MemoryStress Test results can be found at go/cros-mm. FIXUP: CHROMIUM: mm: kstaled: a kswapd alternative Using pmt_t requires including asm/pgtable.h. Also, remove the definition of KSTALED_AGE_PGOFF from include/linux/mm.h and move it to its sole user, kstaled.c. Remove the include of kstaled.h from include/linux/mm.h. Make kstaled related changes in include/linux/mmzone.h dependent on CONFIG_KSTALED, including the include of kstaled.h. That should not normally be necessary, but if the include is conditional there are various compile failures. Include kstaled.h whereever its functions are called, as required by Linux kernel coding style. Disable CONFIG_KSTALED when building vdso32 code for x86_64 target. This patch is not intended to fix any actual problems introduced with kstaled except for the compile problems caused by it on architectures which don't support it. vm_tools: sommelier: A better fix for scaling The previous fix for scaling tried to undo some of the calculations made on the display, but only in the special case of the internal display, it had two drawbacks: - Two wrongs dont make a right - It didnt work for external displays with nonstandard DPI. This is a better fix which solves both problems by scrapping the physical size calculation and instead working backwards from the DPI we want to end up with (which comes from the ideal scale and the conventional DPI). dlcservice: Convert check update_engine status to a getter Dlcservice should only be allowed to install when update_engine is IDLE (which means there is no install or update in progress and no update has been applied). Dlcservice should only be allowed to uninstall when update_engine is IDLE or UPDATED_NEED_REBOOT. It is still valid to uninstall when there has been an update applied, because it will clear the /var/cache to which the update is applied to. This conversion is to provide a finer grain of control in error propagation for each update_engine status. It is clear to see how dlcservice should act for each update_engine status. BUG=chromium:987287 TEST=FEATURES="test" emerge-$B dlcservice TEST=tast run $TEST_IP platform.DLCService Change-Id: Ibd3932fd99c9b4ba32909cfce0e4c5298ed922ae Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1745826 Tested-by: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: firmware: google: check if size is valid when decoding VPD data The VPD implementation from Chromium Vital Product Data project used to parse data from untrusted input without checking if the meta data is invalid or corrupted. For example, the size from decoded content may be negative value, or larger than whole input buffer. Such invalid data may cause buffer overflow. To fix that, the size parameters passed to vpd_decode functions should be changed to unsigned integer (u32) type, and the parsing of entry header should be refactored so every size field is correctly verified before starting to decode.
